---
applyTo: "packages/web-platform/web-bundle-kit/**,packages/rspeedy/plugin-lynx/**,packages/rspeedy/plugin-debug-metadata/**,packages/rspeedy/plugin-react/**,packages/rspeedy/plugin-react-alias/**,packages/webpack/template-webpack-plugin/**,packages/webpack/runtime-wrapper-webpack-plugin/**,packages/webpack/chunk-loading-webpack-plugin/**,packages/webpack/cache-events-webpack-plugin/**,packages/webpack/react-webpack-plugin/**,packages/webpack/css-extract-webpack-plugin/**,packages/webpack/react-refresh-webpack-plugin/**,packages/web-platform/web-core/package.json"
---

`@lynx-js/web-bundle-kit` runs Rsbuild with `pluginLynx` (`@lynx-js/rsbuild-plugin`) and `pluginReactLynx` (`@lynx-js/react-rsbuild-plugin`) on `@rspack/browser` in a Worker. The plugins run there unchanged; do not add browser special cases to them. The kit makes Node.js idioms work instead: `fs` is the memfs of `@rspack/browser`; every bundled module is told its location in a virtual `/node_modules` tree (`import.meta.url`, `import.meta.dirname`, `__dirname`), and the kit mirrors `package.json` files, runtime files and loader placeholders there; `createRequire(...).resolve` resolves against memfs with Rspack's resolver; `createRequire(...)(id)` returns a Node.js built-in stand-in, a module bundled into the kit and registered under the path it resolves to, or a JSON file from memfs. So `require.resolve('./loader.js')` in a static field, `path.resolve(__dirname, './loaders/x')`, `require('../package.json')` and `require(transformPath)` all work in the kit, because the kit imports the plugins only after the mirror is in memfs.

What still breaks the kit: worker pools, child processes and sockets at import time or during a web build (`os.availableParallelism()` is 1 in the kit), `require()` of a package that the kit does not bundle (add it to `REGISTERED` in `web-bundle-kit/rslib.config.ts`), a new loader or runtime file (register the loader; add runtime files compiled into cards to `RUNTIME_FILES` in `scripts/mirror.ts`), and `process.versions.node` checks, which are false in the kit because emnapi under `@rspack/browser` would otherwise take the Worker for Node.js. `LynxEncodePlugin.encodePool` stays a lazy getter that `require()`s tinypool, since tinypool starts threads; `test/encode-pool-lazy.test.ts` guards it. Only the web target can build in a browser: a native `.lynx.bundle` needs the `@lynx-js/tasm` addon. Do not import `@lynx-js/react/transform` statically from `@lynx-js/react-webpack-plugin`: `@lynx-js/react` is its optional peer, and the kit supplies the transform through `require(transformPath)`.

`@lynx-js/web-core/encode` resolves to `dist/encode_prod` (built by rslib for Node, which loads its wasm through `fs`) by default, and to the unbundled `dist/encode` under the `browser` condition, whose `wasm-bindgen --target bundler` glue a browser bundler loads as async WebAssembly. Keep both entries when changing that export.

The kit is built by Rslib from `web-bundle-kit/rslib.config.ts`, one ES module library with everything bundled, like `@rspack/browser` builds itself; the kit's own steps (registered loaders, virtual locations, verbatim functions, `mirror.json`) are transforms and a `processAssets` handler of the plugin in `scripts/plugin.ts`, and must take their virtual paths from the one layout the config computes. Rslib's defaults are for a library that another bundler or Node.js loads; the kit runs as it is in a Worker, so keep these overrides: `output.target: 'web'`, `autoExternal: false`, no minification, `performance.buildCache: false`; `output.library.type: 'module'` with `chunkFormat: 'module'`, because Rslib's `modern-module` writes the export `"module.exports"` of `@rspack/browser` as the member path `.module.exports` in the chunk facade of `import('@rspack/browser')`, which then throws; and the parser options `importDynamic`, `requireDynamic`, `requireAsExpression` and `requireResolve` back on, so that `import(expression)` and `require(expression)` in bundled packages reject with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` instead of fetching a URL or meeting a missing `require`. Keep `createRequire: false` (calls stay calls to the stand-in), define `__non_webpack_require__` as `undefined` (or Rspack turns emnapi's use of it into `import "node:module"`), rewrite `import.meta.*` on the syntax tree, not with a regular expression (Rsbuild contains generated code that mentions `import.meta.url` in strings), keep Rsbuild's own defines (`import.meta.env.*`, `process.env.BASE_URL`, `PUBLIC_*`) out and `optimization.nodeEnv` off (Rslib's default), since the bundled Rsbuild sets `NODE_ENV` for the project at run time, and keep SWC limited to the kit's `src/`. Rsbuild always requires `compiled/html-rspack-plugin`, and css-loader's runtime (`compiled/css-loader/api.js` and friends) is compiled into every card that imports CSS. Mirror the source maps of runtime packages, or every module warns. Rspack stats `loc` columns are 1-based; the code frame `╭─[3:0]` is 0-based.

What each Node.js built-in becomes is the options of `pluginNodePolyfill` (`@rsbuild/plugin-node-polyfill`) in `web-bundle-kit/scripts/builtins.ts`: the plugin's polyfill (`assert`, `events`, `querystring`, `stream`, `string_decoder`, `tty`, `zlib`), an override from `src/node` (the memfs `fs`, `fs/promises` and `Buffer`, `module`, `process`, `crypto`, wrappers that add what bundled code needs to `path`, `url`, `util` and `util/types`, `os`, and traps), or an empty module. `include` must name every built-in, because the plugin ignores overrides for built-ins outside it. The plugin only sets `resolve.fallback`, which loses to an npm package of the same name that a bundled package can reach (pnpm hoists `url`, `util`, `process` and others), so `pluginBuiltinAliases` turns its entries into exact aliases. Keep the plugin's `globals` off: a provided `process` would reach the wasm runtime of `@rspack/browser` before `setup()`. A plugin polyfill that lacks a member bundled code imports by name fails the build only when Rspack can read the CommonJS exports of the package; check the members of a new polyfill against the code that uses it. The overrides in `src/node` are TypeScript ES modules: give each a named export for every member and a default export of the whole module, and list it in `builtinModules` of `src/node/module.ts`. Bundled ES modules that import a missing member fail the kit's build; a CommonJS `require()` of an override gets its namespace, so it sees only the named exports and cannot call the module.

A function whose source text a plugin injects into cards (`Template.getFunctionContent(fn)`, `fn.toString()`, `String(fn)`) must reach the card with the text of the plugin's published file, but bundling the kit rewrites it: Rspack renames `__webpack_require__` to `__nested_rspack_require_<n>_<m>__`, and a minifier would rename everything else. Every module of such functions must be listed in `STRINGIFIED` in `web-bundle-kit/rslib.config.ts`; `scripts/verbatim-functions.ts` then gives each top-level function there a `toString` that returns its published text as a string literal. Today that is `lib/runtime/javascript/*.js` and `lib/runtime/css/*.js` of `@lynx-js/chunk-loading-webpack-plugin` and `lib/runtime/hmr-*.js` of `@lynx-js/react-webpack-plugin`. When a plugin adds a stringified function, put it in a module of its own with only top-level function declarations, and extend `STRINGIFIED` if it lives elsewhere. `Function.prototype.toString.call(fn)` bypasses the override; stringify with `Template.getFunctionContent` or `fn.toString()`.

To check a change to these plugins against the kit, run `pnpm turbo build --filter=@lynx-js/web-bundle-kit`, then `pnpm run test:e2e` (`playwright test`, Chromium with `channel: 'chromium'`) in `packages/web-platform/web-bundle-kit`. It builds a two-card ReactLynx fixture in production and with hot updates, renders it in `<lynx-view>`, applies CSS and TSX hot updates in the rendered development card, compares the `__name__` identifiers of the development cards with a Node.js build of the same fixture, and checks rebuilds and diagnostics. CI runs the Playwright tests of both kits in the `playwright-web-kits` job of `.github/workflows/test.yml`. Only the preview kit reports coverage: `page.coverage` measures the main thread of a page, and the bundle kit runs in a Worker.

The kit's build scripts run on Windows in CI (`Build (Windows)`). Turn real paths into virtual paths, `mirror.json` keys and import specifiers, and compare them with Rspack's resource paths, only through `web-bundle-kit/scripts/paths.ts` (`toPosix`, `relativeSpecifier`, `virtualPathOf`, `pathKey`, `isInside`); give a transform a function condition that uses them instead of a list of paths. `test/paths.test.ts` runs them with `path.win32`. Neither kit is in the root `tsc --build`, because their types need build outputs (the plugins' declarations); they are type-checked by `test:type` after `pnpm turbo build`.
